scores.evidence: Avoid having both systems write at once (dual-write)... move "write authority" over in a single controlled switch.
scores.rationale: Solves the actual problem with an honest definition of no downtime and covers core needs, though it is generic and defers vendor/scale specifics.

scores.evidence: Only the active system may send outbound HL7 appointment (SIU) messages, so the EHR never gets duplicates.
scores.rationale: Single write authority, routing layer, replication direction and interface ownership are applied consistently; minor loose ends like the ordering of interface repointing after writes resume.

scores.evidence: Run at least two full dress rehearsals of the cutover and the rollback, using production-sized data, and time each step.
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to risks (checksums, business checks, shadow reads, rehearsals, go/no-go), but post-launch monitoring and some thresholds (2–3×, 1 sec) are unjustified.

checklist.evidence: sign a BAA (Business Associate Agreement) with the cloud provider, use only HIPAA-eligible services
Make integration endpoints configurable, so the interface engine can be repointed without code changes.
Check row counts and checksums, and also business checks such as "appointments per provider per day match"
Only one system takes bookings at any moment.
Start reverse replication (cloud → on-premises) so the old system stays current for rollback.
Redundant private network links between the hospital and the cloud (e.g., Direct Connect or ExpressRoute), with VPN backup.
with backups and a multi-zone setup for high availability.
Single sign-on tied to your existing directory (AD/Entra), using least-privilege access.
Run the cloud app read-only against the copied data. Replay or mirror real read traffic and compare responses.
Pick the lowest-volume window, typically early on a Sunday morning. Clinical leadership signs off, and the change freeze is in effect.
If this is a vendor product (e.g., Epic Cadence), the vendor's hosting and migration path will drive most of this plan.
